15. In the present matter, though R1 and R2 had not filed their written statement yet, they were given opportunity to cross examinePW2 but, their right to cross examine the petitioner's witnesses was limited to pointing out the falsity or weaknesses of the petitioner's case.

In no circumstances should the cross examination be permitted to travel beyond this legitimate scope and to convert itself virtually into a presentation of respondent's defence either directly or in the form of suggestions put to the petitioner's witnesses.

However, in the present case, the R1 and R2 had tried to put suggestions to PW2 that the alleged accident had taken place due to the sole negligence of the deceased, in driving his motorcycle, which is not permissible.

But, by putting the said suggestion, R1 and R2 had in-fact admitted involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, as they merely stated that the accident had taken place due to the sole negligence of the deceased, in driving his motorcycle.
